Subject: Unexpected slowdown on inference endpoints

Hi Tessa,

We started seeing elevated response times from your hosted inference endpoints this morning around 07:45 PDT. Latencies for /v1/generate are spiking to 6–8s for small prompts that used to be ~300–400ms. This is impacting a critical workflow for our triage app — we have about ~10% errors and many timeouts when we hit our regular QPS.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- API key: (redacted)
- Sample curl: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"short prompt"}'
- First noticed: ~07:45 PDT

Can you confirm if there's a known issue or maintenance window? Please advise next steps — we need ETA and mitigation if possible.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Senior ML Ops, Harbor Clinic

Hi Anika — thank you for the report and the curl sample, this is helpful. I’m escalating immediately and opening an ops bridge with our on-call to investigate. Quick notes:

- We are seeing elevated p95/p99 in us-west-2 for short-sequence generation; our telemetry shows an increase beginning ~07:40 PDT.
- Impact: partial — some requests are delayed, a small fraction retrying clients see timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: we’re enabling a routing policy to divert new traffic to a healthy pool in a different AZ and initiating a lightweight cache warm-up to reduce KV misses.

I’ll post updates here in-thread every 30 minutes until resolved. For now, if you can share any spike timelines or correlated deploys on your side, that would help rule out client-side changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your triage latency.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 08:40:02 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Harbor Clinic — ops update

Team — summary from the bridge so far (internal):

- Root cause hypothesis: a new kernel selection path for short sequences triggered a cache eviction pattern on a subset of hosts in us-west-2; combination of concurrent GC cycle and recent model-quantization tweak caused higher tail latency on a subset of nodes.
- Observed: p50 ~350ms (normal), p95 jumped to ~3.2s, p99 to ~7.1s for the affected pool between 07:40–08:20. Error rate ~1.2% (timeouts).
- Mitigation applied at 08:30: routed ~40% of new traffic away from the affected pool (fallback to compatible quantized variant), disabled the new kernel selector on the affected ASG, and initiated a rolling restart to clear KV cache thrashing.
- Status: visible improvement after routing change; p95 trending down to ~500–700ms for rerouted traffic. Native pool still recovering; ETA for full remediation: 60–90 minutes.

Attached: harbor_incident_log_snippet.txt (short logs from 07:36–08:35 showing retry bursts and eviction messages).

Customer-facing language suggested: short advisory acknowledging elevated response times in us-west-2, note that we applied routing and restarts, provide ETA ~1h, include status page link and offer to follow up with postmortem and credit.

Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 10:30:11 -07:00
Subject: Update: Elevated response times in us-west-2 — resolved & follow-up

Hi Anika / Harbor SRE team —

Update and resolution summary: thank you again for flagging this. We completed remediation and wanted to share findings and next steps.

What happened
- Between 07:40–08:40 PDT on Jul 15 we observed elevated tail latency and a small error rate for short-sequence inference requests in us-west-2. The issue was caused by an interaction between a new kernel-selection path and cache eviction behavior on a subset of hosts, which produced transient KV cache thrashing and GC pressure.

What we did
- Immediately routed traffic away from affected hosts and disabled the new kernel selector for the impacted pool.
- Performed a rolling restart to recover KV caches and cleared the GC pressure.
- Monitored performance until p95/p99 returned to baseline; final validation completed by 09:20 PDT.

Current status
- Service is resolved and healthy in us-west-2. We continue to observe normal latencies (p95 ~350–420ms for the tested short prompts).
- We’ve posted a brief incident notice on our status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2027-07-15-harbor-slow

Next steps / follow-up
- We will deliver a short postmortem document with timelines, root cause analysis, and the corrective actions we will take to prevent recurrence. Draft attached: postmortem-draft.pdf.
- As a goodwill gesture for the outage impact to your production triage workflow, we’d like to offer a one-month service credit applied to July usage — I’ll coordinate details with your billing contact if that’s acceptable.

If you’d prefer a quick call to walk through the postmortem, I’m available today 14:00–16:00 PDT. Please let me know what works.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your patience while we resolved this.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
